messages:
devon: fyi seeing weird p99 token-latency / tokens/sec divergence across regions on the per-token SLI dashboard. west2 p99 jumped but aggregated tokens/sec stayed flat. could be bucketing or prom rule mismatch :thinking:

alice: can you paste the grafana panel link + the prometheus query?

devon: dashboard link -> https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/TokenSLI/per-token-sli?orgId=1&var-region=all
query from panel: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_processing_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, region, model))`

ben: that query looks ok. suspicious things: 1) region label is coming from node exporter vs inference service, 2) we recently changed autoscaler label from `zone` -> `region` which could make some series drop into different buckets.

carol: devon, can you run a quick prom query comparing `count by(region)` of the bucket series? like:
```
count by(region) (token_processing_duration_seconds_bucket)
```

devon: ran it — output shows `region="us-west1"` series count down, `region="us-west2"` count up, total series count unchanged.

infra-bot: ALERT triggered: TokenPipeline.TokenBucketSeriesDrop (severity: warning) — fingerprint f2a9 — see /alerts/1723

alice: that matches label remapping. If the histogram buckets were re-labeled mid-rollout, `histogram_quantile` can report jumps because quantiles are per-series. We should collapse to a consistent label set with a recording rule.

ben: quick mitigation: edit the dashboard panel to use `label_replace` to normalize region labels until we fix the rules. e.g. `label_replace(..., "region", "$1", "zone", "(us-.*)")` or vice-versa depending which is present.

carol: also check KV cache hit-rate correlated? a drop in cache hit could increase latency per token even without tokens/sec changing. query:
```
100 * sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) by(region) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m])) by(region)
```

devon: KV cache miss rate in west2 up 3.7% in the last 10m. Not huge but noticeable.

santiago: cost angle: if p99 jumps but tokens/sec flat, billing looks same but perceived latency SLO breached -> paging. we should suppress noisy p99 alerts until we normalize labeling to avoid oncall churn.

alice: agreed. propose: 1) silence the p99 alert for west2 for 30m with context: "investigating prom label remap" 2) add a recording rule to produce `token_processing_duration_seconds_bucket_v1` with normalized labels 3) backfill graphs to confirm previous values.

devon: i'll open the alert mute now, and start a PR for recording rule. muting alert -> `teams/infra/alerts` modal done :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: Mute applied to `TokenPipeline.P99Latency` in region=us-west2 for 30m by devon.

ben: ping carol if you want me to push a hotfix for the dashboard panel (label_replace) to avoid code churn in prom rules.

carol: if we can reproduce the label flip in a staging cluster, we can test the recording rule before prod rollout. devon, can you pull a 1h range of raw series for `token_processing_duration_seconds_bucket` across both labels?

devon: done. uploaded raw dump to s3://redwood-debug/token-bucket-dumps/1718801123-west2.json.gz

alice: next steps written here: https://docs.internal.redwood/ops/token-sli-labeling -> need owner, ETA 2h for recording rule PR, 6h for rollout + canary.

santiago: one more ask from finance: add a small note on the incident page explaining why p99 spike didn't equal cost spike. that'll avoid cost ops escalations.

devon: noted — adding note and closing loop once recording rule merged. thanks all :thumbsup:
